subject: Post-call recap: quantization trade-offs, recommended evals & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: James Park <james.park@brightwave.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 15:23:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: quantization trade-offs, recommended evals & next steps

Thanks for the intro call today — great to learn more about BrightWave's summarization & code-assist workloads. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can scope a concise POC.

TL;DR
- Primary workload: large-batch summarization of product docs (~2k tokens avg) + code generation prompts for internal developer tools
- Key constraints: latency SLO 200–300ms tail for interactive calls, cost target ~30% below current infra spend, and strict privacy requirements (VPC option)
- Main trade-off discussed: quantization/throughput tuning (AWQ/GPTQ/FP8) vs. generation quality/regression risk

What we recommend next
1) Small eval run: share a representative prompt set (10–20 samples per use-case) with us so we can run side-by-side model + quantization configs and show delta in quality + throughput
2) Suggested initial model candidates: RedDolly-13B-v2 (best cost/perf for batch), Vicuna-2.5-13B (strong instruction-following), and Llama2-70B-CHAT for high-quality baselines
3) Quantization configs to test: AWQ 4-bit (aggressive cost wins), GPTQ 4/8-bit mix (balanced), FP8 (minimal quality loss but higher runtime cost)
4) Deliverables: per-config BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity on your prompts, latency/p95 and tokens/sec, and a short regression report with examples.

Attachments: redwood-quant-tradeoffs.pdf — short overview of AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 tradeoffs (figures + perf table). I also shared an eval prompt template and a sample drive folder link below.

Next steps
- If you can share a small prompt set by Tue (2/17) we’ll queue a focused run and share preliminary results by Fri (2/20)
- Pricing: we can do an initial 1-week eval on Hosted Dedicated credits (no upfront commit) — I’ll follow up with a simple mutual action plan once we confirm scope

Thanks again — cc'ing Priyom to help scope the quantization trade-study and Lukas to align infra/throughput targets.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199

1) For summarization quality, what metrics do you use for "regression"? ROUGE / embedding similarity? Any human eval budget needed?
2) We’re particularly worried about hallucinations on codegen. Does AWQ materially increase hallucination risk vs GPTQ?
3) On delivery: is the POC you mentioned run in our VPC (Private) or your Hosted infra for speed?

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: James Park <james.park@brightwave.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: quantization trade-offs, recommended evals & next steps

Great — thanks for the prompt set, James. That’s exactly what we need to get a quick signal. Below are specific answers and the short plan we’ll run: 

On metrics & human evals
- For summarization we’ll report: ROUGE-L, BERTScore, and embedding cosine similarity (S-BERT) against your reference summaries. We’ll also surface a small human-check of 10–20 examples if you’d like a qualitative sanity check for hallucinations.
- For codegen we’ll run: exact match where applicable, unit-test style execution where feasible, and a manual inspect for hallucination patterns on the 8 code prompts.

AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8 — short guidance
- AWQ (aggressive 4-bit quant): typically gives 2–3x throughput gains vs fp16 with modest quality reduction on many instruction and summarization tasks. It can increase subtle generation artifacts for code-heavy prompts; risk varies by base model and prompt distribution.
- GPTQ (mixed 4/8-bit): safer middle-ground; better preservation of token-level fidelity for codegen while still providing meaningful cost reduction.
- FP8: closest to fp16 quality in most cases but requires hardware that supports efficient FP8 kernels — higher infra cost but lowest quality regression risk.

Planned run (what we’ll deliver)
- Models: RedDolly-13B-v2 (AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 where available), Vicuna-2.5-13B (AWQ/GPTQ), Llama2-70B-CHAT (FP8 baseline)
- Output: per-sample scores + aggregate tables, 10 annotated examples flagged for hallucination risk, latency/p95 and tokens/sec per config, and a short decision recommendation (cost vs quality).
- Timeline: start run Wed 2/18, draft results by Fri 2/20, quick sync the following week for decisioning.

Attachments I’m adding: awq-gptq-trade-study.xlsx (internal perf/quality spreadsheet) and evals-prompt-set.jsonl (our canonical eval template you can use to run locally). Links to results will be posted to the drive folder below as the jobs complete.

POC environment
- We can run the initial eval on our hosted infra for speed and reproducibility. If you prefer the results to reflect your Private/VPC environment, we’ll schedule the same run on your infra (needs a short infra kick-off). Happy to start hosted and re-run 2 top configs in your VPC later.

Next action: Priyom, can you please queue the eval job and confirm expected runtime + credits? James, if you’re good with starting hosted, we’ll proceed on Wed.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: awq-gptq-trade-study.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB stub), evals-prompt-set.jsonl (JSONL, 18KB stub)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: quick note on quantization configs and infra

Marissa / Lukas — quick internal note before we commit compute: 
- I’ll spin the evals on our dedicated GPU pool (A100s w/TF32 and FP8 kernels) to cover FP16/FP8 baselines and GPTQ runs. AWQ runs will use our optimized kernel path (we’ve seen 2.2–2.8x token/sec vs fp16 on 13B models in prior benchmarks).
- For codegen prompts: prioritize GPTQ 4-bit mixed config first to reduce hallucination risks, then AWQ 4-bit for a pure throughput comparison.
- Estimated runtime: 3–4 hours total for the provided sample set across 3 models and 3 configs. Cost covered by evaluation credits for the POC.
- Deliverable: upload raw outputs + per-sample metrics to the drive folder and link the summary doc to the HubSpot deal (BW-2026-031).

I’ll notify when the jobs are queued (ETA Wed 11am PST).

—
Priyom Das
